projects.title: AVION
projects.desc: An autonomous quadcopter that delivers medikits and food parcels to people cut off by floods and landslides. A Raspberry Pi 4 flies the mission through a Pixhawk autopilot, finds colour-marked drop zones with an Intel RealSense D455 depth camera and releases the parcel with a servo hook. A browser ground station with a live 3D digital twin keeps an operator in command of every drop. In-house carbon-fibre and 3D-printed airframe; presented at the ROBOFEST Gujarat 6.0 Hackathon.

chapters.title: The problem
chapters.text: After a flood or a landslide, the people who need help most are the ones a road can no longer reach. AVION is a quadcopter that carries a medikit or a food parcel to a marked drop zone, finds the zone itself and releases the parcel — while an operator on the ground stays in command of every drop.

chapters.title: Airframe
chapters.text: The frame is carbon-fibre tube joined by parts we printed in-house: frame joints, the avionics mounts and the payload hook. Printing our own parts meant a broken joint on the field was a reprint away, not a reorder.

chapters.title: Flight stack
chapters.text: A Pixhawk 2.4.8 running ArduPilot holds the aircraft. A Raspberry Pi 4 sits beside it as the companion computer and flies the mission over MAVLink with DroneKit — take-off, waypoints, search, drop and return.

chapters.title: Perception and the drop
chapters.text: An Intel RealSense D455 gives the Pi depth and colour. OpenCV finds the colour-marked drop zone, the Pi centres the aircraft over it and descends, and a servo hook lets the parcel go.

chapters.title: Ground station
chapters.text: A browser ground station — Flask and Socket.IO behind it, a Three.js digital twin in front — shows the operator the aircraft's attitude and position live, walks them through an operator-checked parcel reload, and runs the whole mission in a browser-based simulator before anything flies.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.text: Every mission was flown in the simulator first: the same ground station, the same waypoints, a virtual aircraft. It caught the mistakes that would have cost an airframe.

chapters.title: Result
chapters.text: AVION reached the finals of ROBOFEST Gujarat 6.0, India's biggest robotics hackathon, organised by GUJCOST at RAC Bhavnagar. The ground station has since grown into AERONEX, a standalone station for ArduPilot aircraft.

projects.title: 4-Bit Microprocessor
projects.sub: Built from discrete logic on breadboards
projects.desc: A fully functional 4-bit microprocessor built entirely from discrete 74-series logic ICs on breadboards. Complete datapath including ALU, registers, instruction register, program counter and shared bus, with a hardwired control unit and a custom instruction set supporting arithmetic, logical, load, store and conditional jump operations.

images.caption: The working processor, wired on breadboards from 74-series logic ICs

projects.title: Dual-Axis CNC Plotter
projects.sub: Motion control from G-code to paper
projects.desc: A 2-axis CNC plotter using Arduino, stepper motors and a custom mechanical frame to translate digital designs into precise physical drawings. Implemented G-code interpretation and motion-control firmware for accurate pen positioning, combining embedded systems with mechanical design.

projects.title: DoseGuard
projects.kind: Decision systems · Nuclear science · Data design
projects.desc: A standards-grounded decision engine for gamma irradiation, built on 30+ IAEA research papers and cross-referenced against each destination country's own regulatory limits (e.g. FDA 21 CFR 179.26). Generates a downloadable, accurate prescription report with tailored recommendations for your exact product and facility. Built for HackAtom Summer University 2026.
